title: [Platform] Fan-out walls: one run per thing, fixed slots, kill switch
goal: Build the walls that stop agent storms: one function that is the only way to start a run (named after the thing it works on, on its agent's own task queue), a slots workflow per agent that lets only a fixed number of VMs run at once, and a kill switch that is read when a run starts and before every step.
outcome: In the Temporal UI, assigning RH-1234 to Nova and then typing /nova RH-1234 shows one run, nova:RH-1234, tagged Agent=nova. With three Nova tickets building, a fourth one waits in line for a slot and starts the moment another run parks or finishes. When a platform engineer turns the kill switch on for nova, new starts are refused, and every open Nova run ends cleanly before its next step with its branch kept.

dependsOn.why: The orchestrator's brokerInternal client (used by workInSandbox) is how the kill-switch check reads the broker. ticketToPr needs it too, so it is merged when G3-24 is.

dependsOn.proof: gh api repos/RhinoHealth/ai-agents/contents/broker/src --jq ".[].name"   # lists the broker sources, including scopes.ts

dependsOn.why: Every run is tagged with the Agent search attribute. Temporal refuses a start that uses an attribute the namespace does not know, so Agent must be registered on namespace ai-agents.
dependsOn.proof: kubectl -n ai-agents exec deploy/temporal-admintools -- temporal operator search-attribute list --namespace ai-agents   # shows Agent  Keyword

dependsOn.why: The third part of the kill switch: bumping an agent's epoch in the LLM gateway kills all its live run tokens. The code in this card works without it, but the switch is not complete until it exists.
dependsOn.proof: Ask the gateway owner how the epoch is bumped today; see the gaps, because no ticket says.

decide.q: Where exactly does the kill switch live, and how does the orchestrator read it? The ticket only says "a row per agent in the broker DB".
decide.owner: The broker owner (G3-07) with the Platform lead.
decide.fallback: One flags table in the broker DB with GET, PUT and DELETE /internal/flags/<name> on the broker's internal port, as in this card. The kill switch is the flag agent:<agent>:stopped, and G5 later stores its routine flags (routine:<name>:paused, routines:fixers:paused) in the same table.

decide.q: Who starts the slots:<agent> workflows, and on which task queue? No ticket says.
decide.fallback: ensureSlots() at worker start, on the housekeeping queue ai-agents-orchestrator, with the USE_EXISTING conflict policy so a restart joins the running ones.

decide.q: How does a person turn the kill switch on before the Slack app has a button for it?
decide.fallback: A platform engineer with inf access port-forwards to the broker's internal port and sends one PUT (the commands are in the steps), then runs the batch stop, then asks the gateway owner for the epoch bump.

decide.q: What does the batch stop pass as the stop signal's "by" argument? The ticket's command has no --input.
decide.owner: The ticketToPr owner (G3-24 and G3-38 define the stop signal).

decide.q: One worker process for all eight task queues, or one deployment per queue?
decide.fallback: One orchestrator-worker deployment with 2 replicas, as G3-17 sets, running eight Worker objects that share one connection and one workflow bundle.

files.what: The only way to start a run. startRun builds the ID <agent>:<thing> and the queue ai-agents-<agent>, joins an open run with USE_EXISTING, tags the run with Agent, and refuses to start when the kill switch is on. startOrSignal is the signal-with-start form for routines that join a run by root cause (G5-09 uses it).

notes.text: A typed key for the Agent search attribute. Keyword means an exact-match tag you can filter on.
Callers can catch this and skip. The Jira poll must do that, or its activity retries forever (see the gaps).
Conflict policy: what a start does while a run with this ID is open. USE_EXISTING returns the open run instead of failing.
Reuse policy: about closed runs. A root cause whose run already finished may not start again; a person looks instead.
One signal argument (a Trigger for routines). The SDK's types need a fixed tuple here, so the helper takes one value.

files.what: Reads a flag from the broker's flag store through G3-20's brokerInternal client. null means the flag is not set.
One shared Temporal client per process (G3-28's sketch already calls temporalClient()). Create it only if it is not there yet.

The slots workflow, one per agent, ID slots:<agent>. It keeps a list of holders and a line of waiting runs, grants a slot by signal, takes slots back from runs that died without giving them back, and continues as new when Temporal suggests it (continue-as-new starts a fresh history with the same ID, so the history never grows too large).

notes.text: VMs in parallel per agent, to start with. Raising one is a one-line PR.
A retried request must not take a second place in line.
A run that is stopped while it waits leaves the line.
The SDK says when the history is getting long; better than counting events by hand.
Runs only after an hour with nobody granted. A terminated run skips its finally block, so without this its slot is lost forever.
The run ended while it waited in line. Without this catch, the slots workflow itself fails and every run of this agent waits forever.

files.what: How a run holds a slot: takeSlot before acquireSandbox and before wakeSandbox, giveSlot after parkSandbox and after releaseSandbox. withSlot wraps a whole step. The ticket puts these in slots.ts; they are split only to keep each file short.

notes.text: Set the handler before asking, so a fast grant is never missed.
If the run is cancelled while in line, it tells the slots workflow to forget it.
Giving the slot back must happen even when the run is being cancelled.

files.what: The workflow-side check. killed(agent) runs a local activity (an activity that runs inside the same worker, without a round trip through the task queue), so reading the switch before every step costs milliseconds.
The two activities behind the walls: agentStopped reads the kill switch flag; stillOpen asks Temporal which slot holders are still running. Export both from activities/index.ts.

notes.text: Only "this run does not exist" frees a slot. Any other error (Temporal busy) keeps the holder.

files.what: The flag store in the broker: a flags table created at broker start and three internal routes. Mount flagRoute on the internal listener next to POST /internal/runs, never on the sandbox-facing port, and write each PUT and DELETE to the broker's existing audit log.

notes.text: Only names of this shape are accepted, so a typo cannot create a flag nobody reads.
Every switch says who turned it on and why; the Slack alert and the runbook show it.

files.what: The orchestrator-worker entry point (ts_platform.md runs dist/main.js). One Temporal worker per task queue, all sharing one connection and one workflow bundle, and ensureSlots() so every slots:<agent> workflow exists before any run asks for a slot. If G3-24 already created main.ts, merge these lines into it.

notes.text: One queue per agent, plus ai-agents-orchestrator for housekeeping, so a storm of one agent cannot take the workers another agent needs.
Bundle the workflow code once; eight Worker.create calls with workflowsPath would bundle it eight times at start.
Before any run starts: a run that signals a slots workflow that does not exist fails.

files.what: The change to G3-24's ticketToPr: take a slot before claiming a VM, give it back when the VM is parked or released, take it again before waking, and read the kill switch before the plan step and the build step. The diff is written against G3-24's sketch; apply the same idea to the real file.

Three tiny workflows for the tests, bundled together with the real slots workflow: one that stays open, one that holds a Nova slot until told "done", and one with three steps and a kill-switch check before each.

The three tests the ticket asks for, with TestWorkflowEnvironment.createLocal (a real local dev server with the Agent attribute registered) and a fake flag store. These tests were run against Temporal SDK 1.24.0 and pass.

notes.text: Replace the broker call with a set of names, so the tests need no broker and no database.
Four runs ask at the same moment, so which one waits is not known in advance. Find it, do not assume it is the 4th.
The fake step 1 turns the switch on, so the run must stop before step 2 and never run it.

gaps: Nobody starts the slots:<agent> workflows (also in TICKET_ISSUES.md). If they do not exist, the first takeSlot signal fails and the run fails. Recommendation: ensureSlots() at worker start on ai-agents-orchestrator with USE_EXISTING, as in main.ts here.

The sketch's slots workflow signals slotGranted with no error handling. If the run at the front of the line ended while it waited, the signal throws, the slots workflow fails, and every later run of that agent waits forever. This card catches the error and drops that holder.

A run that is terminated (not cancelled) never runs its finally block, so in the sketch its slot is never given back and the agent permanently loses capacity (Nova has only 3). This card adds an hourly stillOpen check that takes back slots from runs that are no longer running.

The sketch lets one run stand in line twice (a retried request). This card ignores a request from a run that already holds a slot or is already waiting, and also removes a run from the line when it releases while still waiting.

withSlot(agent, fn) alone cannot give the slot back while the VM is parked, because parking happens inside the step. The ticket says a parked run gives its slot back, so this card adds takeSlot and giveSlot and calls them around parkSandbox and wakeSandbox in ticketToPr.
The batch stop command in the ticket has no --input, but the stop signal takes a "by" argument (also in TICKET_ISSUES.md). Recommendation: --input '"kill-switch"'.

G3-24's sketch never sets a handler for the stop signal (TICKET_ISSUES.md), so until G3-38 adds it, the batch stop is buffered and does nothing. In this card the per-step kill-switch check is what really ends the runs.

The kill switch is "a row per agent in the broker DB", but no ticket defines the table, the endpoint, or who may write it. G3-17's NetworkPolicy lets only orchestrator-worker reach the broker's internal port, so neither a person nor the Slack app can flip it directly. Recommendation: the flags table and routes in this card, a port-forward for people until the Slack app gets a button that goes through the orchestrator.

G0-13 says bumping an agent's epoch kills its gateway tokens, but no ticket says where the epoch is stored or how it is bumped (no endpoint, no store). Until the gateway owner answers, the kill switch has two of its three parts; run tokens still die with each run.

startRun now throws AgentStopped while the switch is on. G3-28's startMatches calls startRun inside an activity whose retry policy has no attempt limit, so it would retry forever. Recommendation for G3-28: catch AgentStopped and skip (or check the switch once per poll before the loop).
G3-20 uses brokerInternal but no ticket names its file. This card imports it from orchestrator/src/broker-internal.ts; change the import if it lives elsewhere.

G3-29 asks for patched() around any new workflow step. The ticketToPr change here adds signals and local activities, so it would break the replay of runs that started before the deploy. Before the pilot (G4-28) no Nova run is open in production, so plain code is fine; if any run is open when this deploys, wrap the new lines in patched("g3-25-slots").

No ticket sets a PR title format for the ai-agents repo. fcp uses "[FE] RH-6589: ..." and add-jira-links reads the Jira key from the title. Recommendation: "[Platform] RH-<n>: ..." with this ticket's Jira key once it is filed.
pr: Title: "[Platform] RH-<n>: Fan-out walls: one run per thing, slots, kill switch" (no ticket fixes the format for ai-agents; this follows fcp's style).

Paste the fan-out test output (# pass 3) into the PR body, and say whether the replay test needed patched().
Say in the body which decisions you took the fallback for (flag store, who starts slots, the batch-stop input).
No change under .github/ or the other protected paths in settings/protected-paths.yaml.

rollback: Revert the PR and redeploy orchestrator-worker and the broker; the flags table can stay, because nothing reads it any more. If runs started with the new code are still open, stop them with the batch stop first, then end the slots workflows with: temporal workflow terminate --namespace ai-agents --query 'WorkflowType="slots"' --reason "G3-25 rollback".
prompt:
You are helping Sean do ticket G3-25 ("Fan-out walls: one run per thing, fixed slots, kill switch") in the RhinoHealth/ai-agents repo (TypeScript on Node 24, npm workspaces, ESM with .js import paths, node:test through tsx, exact-pinned dependencies).

Goal: every run starts through one function (startRun / startOrSignal in orchestrator/src/fanout.ts) with the ID <agent>:<thing>, the queue ai-agents-<agent>, the Agent search attribute and USE_EXISTING; a slots:<agent> workflow per agent hands out VM slots (nova 3, cifix 2, upgrade 2, flaky 1, bugfix 2, health 1, security 1); a kill switch (flag agent:<agent>:stopped in the broker's flag store) is read by startRun and before every workflow step.

Start from the card: ~/Projects/ai-agents-course/content/cards/G3-25.json. Its files[].code.text holds tested code for orchestrator/src/{fanout,flags,temporal,main}.ts, orchestrator/src/workflows/{slots,with-slot,kill-switch}.ts, orchestrator/src/activities/fanout.ts, broker/src/flags.ts, a diff for ticket-to-pr.ts, and the tests. Read the real repo first and adapt the code to it (for example where brokerInternal really lives, how the broker routes its internal port, what ticketToPr really looks like). Read the card's "decide" and "gaps" lists; where a decision is still open, use the fallback and tell me.

Walls (do not cross):
- Workflow code stays deterministic: no Node APIs, no fetch, no Date.now() for logic; all I/O in activities.
- Only the orchestrator starts runs. Nothing reachable from a VM may start a run.
- No maxTurns, budgets or time limits on agents. Timeouts are safety nets only.
- Do not touch .github/ or anything in settings/protected-paths.yaml.
- Do not commit, push or open a PR; show me the diff when you are done.
- If you use subagents, use at most two and tell them not to start their own.

Done when:
1. `node --import tsx --test orchestrator/test/fanout.test.ts` prints "# pass 3" and "# fail 0" (the test starts a local dev server; the temporal CLI is installed).
2. `npm run check` is green.
3. `grep -rn "workflow.start(\|signalWithStart(" orchestrator/src slack-app/src` shows only fanout.ts and ensureSlots in main.ts.
4. You list which "decide" fallbacks you used and anything in the repo that did not match the card.
